paper: Vacca M et al. 2024, Nat Metab 6:1178
verified_source_and_location: Full text read in Phase 1 (research/roadmap_phase1/paper_methods_matrix.csv; Figs 3-5)
input_representation: Model-vs-matched-control fold changes per gene and per pathway; human MASLD stage signatures
prediction_target_or_output: Ranking of murine diet models by proximity to human MASLD
feature_construction_selection: Restrict to human-significant genes/pathways; quantile normalisation + ComBat across facilities (design not confounded)
model_family_and_reason: No ML; direction agreement + hypergeometric enrichment
quantitative_evaluation: Direction agreement vs chance; enrichment p
key_result: Whole-transcriptome direction agreement near chance; agreement improves when restricted to significant genes and at pathway level
limitations: Needs matched controls per study; restriction uses significance in the human target
transferable_to_our_gene_effect_task: PARTLY: supports comparing signed reference effects gene-wise and expecting pathway-level agreement to be stronger. Restricting to target-significant genes would be LEAKAGE in our prediction task
how_used_in_phase4b: Motivates block B (prior pathway membership) and the warning that gene-level agreement is weak; we do NOT restrict to PE-significant genes

paper: Liberzon A et al. 2015, Cell Syst 1:417
verified_source_and_location: Full text (PMC) read 2026-11-22: Introduction and Results ('50 hallmarks... comprise 4,022 of the original 8,380 MSigDB gene sets'; 'reducing both variation and redundancy')
input_representation: Curated gene sets (refined from founder sets)
prediction_target_or_output: Gene set collection for enrichment analysis
feature_construction_selection: Computational clustering of founder sets + expert curation; coherent expression
key_result: 50 sets summarise most founder-set information with less redundancy
limitations: Hallmarks still overlap; designed for enrichment, not as predictive features
transferable_to_our_gene_effect_task: YES as an EXTERNAL, PE-independent annotation: gene membership can be a binary gene feature
how_used_in_phase4b: Source of most block-B memberships (frozen list in feature_engineering_plan.md)

paper: Foroutan M et al. 2018, BMC Bioinf 19:404 (singscore)
verified_source_and_location: Full text (PMC) read 2026-11-22: Background/Results ('scores obtained by GSVA, z-score, PLAGE and ssGSEA can be unstable when less data are available (NS < 25)'; singscore 'stable regardless of the composition and number of samples')
feature_construction_selection: Rank-based score of signature genes within each sample
validation_splitting: Cancer data sets; permutation null per sample
quantitative_evaluation: Stability vs sample number; separation of phenotypes
key_result: Single-sample scores stable in small data sets
transferable_to_our_gene_effect_task: NO for our current target (rows = genes). Would require a different task with SAMPLES as rows (e.g. per-mouse programme scores); not run
how_used_in_phase4b: Cited to explain why sample-level scores are not added as gene columns

paper: Hanzelmann S, Castelo R, Guinney J 2013, BMC Bioinf 14:7 (GSVA)
verified_source_and_location: Full text (PMC) read 2026-11-22: Results ('estimates variation of pathway activity over a sample population in an unsupervised manner'; KS-like rank statistic; kernel CDF)
prediction_target_or_output: Gene set x sample enrichment matrix
feature_construction_selection: Unsupervised; kernel CDF per gene then KS-like statistic per set
model_family_and_reason: n/a; downstream differential pathway activity and survival models
quantitative_evaluation: Detection power vs other GSE methods
key_result: Transforms expression into pathway-activity matrix for downstream models
limitations: Depends on sample population; unstable at small n (per Foroutan 2018)
transferable_to_our_gene_effect_task: NO for current target; same reason as singscore

paper: Schubert M et al. 2018, Nat Commun 9:20 (PROGENy)
verified_source_and_location: Full text (PMC) read 2026-11-22: Results/Methods ('208 publicly available experiment series'; 'top 100 genes per pathway'; 'z-scores from a single experiment perform no better than random'; leave-one-out benchmark; TCGA survival, GDSC drug response)
input_representation: Perturbation-experiment z-scores (gene x pathway weight matrix); sample expression
unit_of_observation: SAMPLE (pathway scores); model built across hundreds of experiments
feature_construction_selection: Linear model of gene z-scores on perturbed pathway; top-100 responsive genes; matrix multiplication
model_family_and_reason: Linear regression; chosen for interpretability of footprint weights
validation_splitting: Leave-one-out over perturbation experiments; external associations (drivers, drug response, survival)
key_result: Consensus footprints from many experiments beat single-experiment signatures
limitations: Cancer signalling pathways (human), not liver metabolic states; mouse version exists but not for fasting/MASH/PPARa states
transferable_to_our_gene_effect_task: CONCEPT YES, METHOD NO: our references ARE single-experiment footprints, which PROGENy shows are noisy -> motivates reliability-aware shrinkage (block A). PROGENy pathway weights could be gene features only for signalling pathways irrelevant to our axes
how_used_in_phase4b: Motivates block A; PROGENy weights not used

verified_source_and_location: Full text read in Phase 1 (Figs 3-4, Table 3)
input_representation: Per-study effect sizes (Hedges' g) and SEs
prediction_target_or_output: Pooled DE genes vs silver standard
key_result: Effect-size thresholds (~1.2-1.3 fold) and multi-study pooling increase reproducibility; BH q-values underestimate false positives
transferable_to_our_gene_effect_task: PARTLY: supports inverse-variance weighting and shrinking noisy single-study effects (block A); pooling across our references is NOT valid (different states)
how_used_in_phase4b: Motivates block A and Phase 4 weights

paper: Lee E et al. 2008, PLoS Comput Biol 4:e1000217
verified_source_and_location: Full text (PMC) read 2026-11-22: Abstract/Results ('classifiers using pathway activity achieve better performance than classifiers based on individual gene expression'; CORGs; 'markers ... selected using the whole first dataset and then tested on the second dataset'; AUC)
input_representation: Gene expression vs pathway activity (mean of condition-responsive genes)
feature_construction_selection: Pathway activity from CORGs selected for discriminative power within training data
model_family_and_reason: Logistic-type classifiers; pathway features to reduce redundancy and improve robustness
validation_splitting: Within-dataset CV and CROSS-DATASET (train on one study, test on another)
key_result: Pathway-level features outperformed gene-level markers, including across datasets
limitations: CORG selection uses class labels (must stay inside training); sample-level task
transferable_to_our_gene_effect_task: NO directly (sample-level classification). Supports the IDEA that pathway structure adds robustness; in our gene-row task the analogue is pathway MEMBERSHIP as a gene feature (block B), not CORG scores
how_used_in_phase4b: Rationale for block B; pathway-level sample task listed as a separate future task

verified_source_and_location: NOT re-verified in Phase 4B (publisher bot check; not bypassed). Cited from Phase 4 for the general principle of blocked CV
key_result: Random CV underestimates error under dependence; blocking recommended
limitations: Blocks must reflect dependence; can be conservative
transferable_to_our_gene_effect_task: YES: we block genes by external co-expression modules (and chromosomes in sensitivity)

paper: Li Q et al. 2025, Sci Rep 15:2583 (PS liver)

input_representation: Liver RNA-seq DEGs (|log2FC|>1, adj p<0.05) per PS size vs H2O
feature_construction_selection: Venn overlap of DEG lists; STRING network; CytoHubba rankings
